evidence.note: Opened with a distinct parse/inspect stage: listed files, extracted exact node/edge counts for all four graphs and the reference alignment format/length, establishing the first milestone before any coding.

Built score.py (S3+NC implementation) and immediately measured the reference alignment (S3=0.248) and greedy baseline (S3=0.031) — scorer constructed and baseline measured before optimizing, the sensible milestone ordering the level-8 anchor describes.

Consistently used numeric done-criteria tied to thresholds: derived required Ea/E2 to reach S3>=0.55 and tracked NC>=0.30 as a separate gate; treated yeast (S3>=0.55,NC>=0.30) and DM-HS (S3>=0.32) as distinct goals with their own targets.

Repeatedly deferred the 'easier' DM-HS deliverable ('also need DM-HS') but left it essentially unattempted until the final steps (S3=0.010). Effort was not budgeted across deliverables by difficulty — argues against the level-10 anchor.

End-phase: measured both files against thresholds and gated the 'complete' decision on those measured scores (yeast 0.396/NC0.50, DM-HS 0.010), confirming score-gated milestone tracking persisted through the whole arc despite heavy script thrashing.

reasoning: The agent sequenced genuine, numerically-gated milestones — parse → build S3/NC scorer → measure reference & greedy baselines → optimize toward explicit thresholds — and tracked the two deliverables with their distinct S3/NC targets throughout, squarely matching the level-8 anchor (scorer built before optimizing, each stage with a numeric done-check). It falls short of level 10 because effort was poorly budgeted across the two tasks (the S3-only DM-HS deliverable was neglected until the final steps and never optimized) and fallbacks were reactive thrashing rather than pre-planned per-milestone branches.
